clue.text: Gets, when catching cold, some paper

indicators.note: catching means the word for when takes the other pieces inside it, as a net catches fish

parts.note: as means when, as in 'she waved as he left'
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
a quire is a set quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold coming on picks up a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' is not about falling ill: the two-letter word for 'when' opens up and swallows the cold and the paper, ending as the answer's first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to obtain or come to own something.

clue.text: A sign of island produce

parts.note: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples
corn is farm produce, a grain crop

explanation.surface: Fruit and vegetables on a stall tell you which island you are on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' is a sign of the zodiac, and 'produce' is the noun for what a farm grows, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the goat is one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac.

clue.text: America's broken-down area

parts.note: U/S is an abbreviation for unserviceable, said of machinery that is out of order
A is the abbreviation for area in formulas

explanation.surface: A run-down district of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: US here is not the country but the old services abbreviation u/s, unserviceable, describing kit that no longer works.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: the initials of the nation commonly called by that name.

clue.text: Come down heavy in a petty way?

definitions.text: Come down heavy in a petty way?

parts.words: Come down heavy in a petty way?
parts.note: petty is a joke adjective meaning to do with pets; what comes down heavily is a downpour, named in an idiom after two household animals

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for pouring very hard, with 'petty' punning on the two domestic animals it names.

clue.text: Joint lovers turned up in shock

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the two words run together are read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a joint is slang for a disreputable place, a den
nuts are enthusiasts, as in 'football nuts' who love the game

explanation.surface: A couple who share everything arrive in a state of trauma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads DEN followed by NUTS, seven letters in all, from the bottom upwards. 'Joint' is a noun here, a seedy place, not 'shared'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dazed, as after a blow or bad news.

clue.text: Christmas Eve revellers will keep sober

indicators.note: will keep says these three words hold the answer inside them as a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: Partygoers on 24 December promise, improbably, to stay off the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of plain and austere, as in a sober dark suit.

clue.text: This — giant cross, but in rocks

indicators.note: something that rocks is shaken about, so the letters of the four words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A huge crucifix is pointed out, oddly set among boulders.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash is not punctuation but part of the definition: it is a picture of the answer. 'rocks' is a verb, shaking up the fifteen letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture: the printed dash is itself the mark used for taking one number from another.

clue.text: Winning letter repeated for writer?

parts.note: the letter is the one Churchill made a wartime sign of triumph; spelling it out in the 'A for apple' style writes that letter twice

explanation.definitionFit: Wartime slogan: the letter stands for triumph, and written out in full the slogan shows that letter twice.

clue.text: Sculptor grinding surface edges away

indicators.note: edges away tells you to drop the first and last letters of the word for wearing down

parts.note: eroding is wearing away a surface by grinding at it

explanation.surface: An artist in stone files the sharp corners off a rough face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges away' removes the first and last letters of ERODING. The surface is not ground down in the answer; 'grinding surface' is just a description of erosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Auguste, the Frenchman who made The Thinker and The Kiss.

clue.text: Film with Harlow cast in lead, plot about drug?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the word for drug
to cast is to throw, so the letters of the three words after it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to drug is to numb, to deaden feeling

explanation.surface: A movie starring Jean Harlow, whose story concerns narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast in lead' reads as movie talk about the star, but 'cast' throws ten letters into the order PLATILONDE, and 'about' wraps that round the word for drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the 1931 Frank Capra comedy that gave Jean Harlow her nickname.

clue.text: There's nothing like returning short version of letter

indicators.note: returning means the letters built from nothing and like are read back to front

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: short means the word like loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A postal service admits that nothing beats sending back a brief note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims LIKE to LIK, and 'returning' turns O plus LIK back to front. The letter is one of the alphabet, not a piece of post.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the code word used for K in the NATO spelling alphabet.

clue.text: Not bothered by success, rogues cycling

indicators.note: bothered means disturbed, so the letters of the word before it are put out of order

parts.note: a wow is a great success, as in 'the show was a wow'
heels are cads, contemptible men, in dated slang

explanation.surface: Scoundrels on bikes ride on, unmoved by their win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' rearranges NOT into ONT. 'Not bothered' reads as 'unconcerned', and 'cycling', often a signal to rotate letters, is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive phrase: riding a bike means travelling on a pair of them.

clue.text: During rally, most of net to break

indicators.note: during means the shortened word sits inside the word for rally

parts.note: to rally is to convene, to come together

indicators.note: most of means the word for net loses its last letter

parts.note: a net is a trap for catching fish or animals

explanation.surface: In a long tennis exchange, nearly the whole net gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rally' is a verb, to gather, not a tennis exchange, and the 'net' is one for catching things; 'most of' drops its last letter before 'During' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to infringe a rule or law.

clue.text: Ultimately, where mafia got put away

indicators.note: ultimately tells you to take the final letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: The prison where the mobsters finally ended up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' suggests being jailed, but it means to consume food.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to put food away is to consume it.

clue.text: Having ribs, fish will retain shape

indicators.note: will retain says the fish holds the word for shape inside it

parts.note: cod is a common food fish
shape means state or condition, as in 'in good shape'

explanation.surface: A fish with a bony frame keeps its form when cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical term from the Latin for rib: ridged or ribbed.

clue.text: Court welcomes longing for distinction

indicators.note: welcomes means the abbreviation for court takes the word for longing inside it

parts.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court in addresses
an ache is a longing, a yearning

explanation.surface: A royal household embraces those who yearn for honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: prestige, the quality of being admired.

clue.text: Does one turn out to protect a force for good?

indicators.note: to protect means the word for one who turns things out wraps round the other two letters

parts.note: to evert is to turn outwards or inside out, so one who does it is an everter
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: Will somebody show up to guard a police unit that does the right thing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts A and F inside EVERTER, a whimsical noun for someone who turns things inside out. 'for good' means permanently, not for virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean always from now on, as fairy tales end.

clue.text: A transplanted organ for rabbit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: transplanted means moved to a new place, so the letters of the next word are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A vet gives a pet bunny a new kidney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transplanted' is surgery in the surface but signals the anagram, giving the letters NGORA after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-haired breed kept for its soft wool.

clue.text: Top mark is the target

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, top quality, and the figure 1 is written as the letter I
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A student is aiming for the highest grade.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first class, is written AI in crosswords, the figure 1 standing as a capital I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the goal one is trying to reach.

clue.text: Hostage is held in flat? Right

indicators.note: held in means the word is sits inside the word for flat

parts.note: prone means lying flat, face down
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kidnap victim is being kept in an apartment, the police confirm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is the adjective, lying face down, not a British apartment; 'held in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a captive held against their will.

clue.text: Spiritual "style" of "gangnam style"?

indicators.note: of makes the stylishness belong to the singer, so his name comes first and the word for style follows

parts.note: Gangnam Style was the 2012 worldwide hit by the South Korean singer Psy
chic means style, elegance

explanation.surface: A gospel song done in the manner of a Korean pop hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'style' of the man behind Gangnam Style would be his chic, with his stage name in front. 'Spiritual' is an adjective, not a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: concerned with the mind or soul rather than the body.

clue.text: Israeli politician's son — he'd always put in complaint

indicators.note: put in means the three short pieces are placed inside the word for complaint

parts.note: a moan is a complaint, a grumble
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
taken as written, without its apostrophe
ay is an old or poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A minister's boy who was forever lodging grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is the container signal; 'always' gives its old poetic form, and the apostrophe of 'he'd' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the eye-patched general who became defence and foreign minister.

clue.text: One of the glands (they're all the same)

definitions.meaning: a female reproductive gland that produces eggs
a joke reading in two parts: a round letter standing for zero, then a verb meaning differ, so none of them differ

explanation.surface: An anatomy student shrugs that one gland is much like another.
explanation.definitionFit: The female egg-producing organ is a gland, and its name splits into zero plus a verb meaning differ.

clue.text: Student group's desire to take November off

indicators.note: to take something off is to remove it, so the letter for November comes away from the word for desire

parts.note: to yearn is to desire strongly
November is the NATO alphabet word for N

explanation.surface: A class of undergraduates would love a month's holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: all the pupils who started school together form one.

clue.text: Do a runner?

parts.note: do is a hairdo and the runner is a boy who carries messages in a hotel, so this is a hairstyle named after him; to do a runner is British slang for fleeing

explanation.definitionFit: Pun: a smooth bobbed style named after a hotel's errand lad, a 'do' for a 'runner'.

clue.text: Some music appears to be better

indicators.note: some says only part of the two words after it is wanted, a run of consecutive letters

explanation.surface: Certain tunes just sound superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here: to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to outdo or surpass something.

clue.text: My old relative's reaction to bright light

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old, as in OE for Old English
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: An elderly aunt of mine squints at the glare.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term: narrowing of the pupil of the eye, which glare brings on.

clue.text: Plan to have double-cross on church tower

indicators.note: on means the swindle is added in front of the tower, the two side by side

parts.note: to con is to swindle or double-cross
a spire is the tall pointed tower of a church

explanation.surface: A scheme to mount a second crucifix on the steeple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double-cross' is a betrayal, not two crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to plot together in secret.
